On linux/windowx x86, this means the "cpu" runner is actually the main ollama executable (without AVX) and then cpu_avx and cpu_avx2 are discrete secondary binaries with the respective vector flags turned on.  When you set the custom flags at build time, the assumption is there's no reason to waste time or space to build alternative cpu vector features, so we just build the main binary with the flags you have requested.  I'm not sure what your objective is on the build you're setting up, but if you set the custom cpu flags and then try to run the ollama executable on a system without those features, it will crash with illegal instruction errors.  If you're aiming to support the permutations, you could do the build in two steps, setting the custom flags for just the GPU runners, and then omit the flag for the cpu runner(s) so you get the 3 variations and the main binary remains without any AVX* flags.
